summary: Same scene, same order, all facts, negations and causal links intact; all five comprehension questions answerable. One voice drift in Michael's opening condescension (b019 'ik begrijp het wel.'), the rest are notes.

comprehension.q: What does Michael say in reply to Petunia, and what does his tone give away?
comprehension.answer_from_nl: He says 'Je maakt een grapje'; his tone says otherwise: he is very afraid — maybe she really means it.

comprehension.q: According to Michael, how could what Petunia saw have been faked, and what name does he give to the trick of seeming to guess someone's thoughts?
comprehension.answer_from_nl: A trained stage magician (goochelaar) easily imitates something that only seems impossible — he taught Harry to bend spoons; if it seemed they could always guess your thoughts, that is called cold reading.

comprehension.q: What did Lily do to Petunia, and why did Lily do it?
comprehension.answer_from_nl: Lily made Petunia the way she is now (her slim body); because Petunia begged her, for years.

comprehension.q: Why did Petunia beg Lily for years — what had she felt about Lily, and what did she want even though she could not have magic?
comprehension.answer_from_nl: Lily had always been prettier; Petunia had been mean to her because of that; then Lily got magic too. She begged Lily to use some of that magic on her so she would also be pretty — she could not get the magic, but she could at least be pretty.

comprehension.q: What had Petunia told Lily and her husband about Michael, and why can't she just tell Michael what she saw?
comprehension.answer_from_nl: She had told them Michael was not allowed to know. She can't just tell him because then he will think she is— (unfinished).

findings.fragment: Lieverd, ik begrijp het wel. Je kent de sceptische literatuur niet.
findings.problem: The full stop plus 'wel' turn a dry statement of her ignorance ('I understand that you're not familiar with…') into a reassuring 'I do understand' followed by a separate diagnosis; what he understands is no longer her unfamiliarity but, by implication, why she believes this.
findings.evidence: EN: 'Dear, I understand that you're not familiar with the sceptical literature.' vs NL: 'Lieverd, ik begrijp het wel. Je kent de sceptische literatuur niet.'
findings.required_fix: Drop 'wel' and bind the two halves so that 'het' is her unfamiliarity: 'Lieverd, ik begrijp het: je kent de sceptische literatuur niet.'

findings.problem: 'iets anders' spells out the contrast between his words and his tone that the English leaves for the reader to notice.
findings.evidence: EN: 'His tone indicated that he was very much afraid that she was serious.' vs NL: 'Zijn toon zei iets anders: hij was heel bang. Misschien meende ze het echt.'
findings.required_fix: Optional. A frame that reports rather than contrasts, e.g. 'Zijn toon verried hem: hij was heel bang.' The split itself and 'Misschien meende ze het echt.' are fine; the link survives by sentence order.

findings.fragment: Ze wees naar zichzelf, blijkbaar naar haar slanke lichaam.
findings.problem: 'blijkbaar' (evidently) is a firmer inference than the narrator's tentative 'as though to indicate', and 'wees naar' narrows a gesture at her whole figure to pointing.
findings.evidence: EN: 'She gestured at herself, as though to indicate her lithe form.' vs NL: 'Ze wees naar zichzelf, blijkbaar naar haar slanke lichaam.'
findings.required_fix: Optional: 'Ze gebaarde naar zichzelf, naar haar slanke lichaam, zo leek het.'

findings.fragment: De professor rolde met zijn ogen.
findings.problem: The narrator's label for Michael is 'de Professor' with a capital P (bible, glossary); lowercase weakens the visible switch from 'Michael' to the ironic label at the moment he starts lecturing.
findings.evidence: bible: 'Exception: de Professor (capital P) when the narrator uses it as Michael's label'; NL: 'De professor rolde met zijn ogen.'
